title: Muse, Meta's extraordinarily privileged AI assistant, has a serious 0-day
gist: macOS security researcher Patrick Wardle disclosed a zero-day in Meta's Muse AI assistant letting any local app or terminal command hijack the account-authentication token by redirecting its cloud transcription endpoint, giving full agent control (file writes, camera access, WhatsApp exfiltration) via a simple ClickFix attack; Amazon has separately begun blocking Muse from shopping on its site.

insights.claim: Meta's Muse AI assistant contains a zero-day vulnerability discovered by macOS security researcher Patrick Wardle that lets any locally installed app or terminal command, regardless of its own macOS permissions, change an undocumented setting controlling where Muse's voice transcription is sent, redirecting it to an attacker-controlled server to steal the account authentication token.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: A full-account-takeover zero-day in a widely-hyped 'secure by design' AI assistant is a concrete data point that agentic AI assistants with broad OS/account permissions carry outsized security risk versus their utility, relevant to enterprise AI-agent adoption risk assessment.
insights.quote: We can manipulate the agent and leverage its privileges to do whatever we want. So instead of us having to write a very comprehensive Mac malware stealer, we can just leverage the AI assistant itself.
insights.locator: Patrick Wardle, the macOS security expert who discovered the zero-day, told Ars

insights.claim: A single simple ClickFix attack (a technique already known to be effective at tricking users into infecting their own devices) combined with a terminal command is sufficient to give an attacker permanent control of a victim's Muse account, with the token automatically sent to the attacker's proxy server.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: The low attack complexity (no advanced exploit chain needed) means this vulnerability is easily weaponizable at scale, raising urgency for a Meta patch and for enterprises to restrict Muse deployment until fixed.
insights.locator: A single ClickFix is all it takes

insights.claim: Wardle identified two specific Meta design flaws enabling the exploit: choosing to process Muse dictation/transcription in the cloud (where Meta logs it) rather than on-device as macOS natively supports, and allowing any app to control all of Muse's undocumented settings including the sensitive transcription-endpoint setting, rather than restricting apps to only UI-level controls.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Both flaws were avoidable using existing, safer macOS-native alternatives, suggesting the vulnerability stems from a security-versus-speed tradeoff in Muse's development rather than an unavoidable technical limitation.
insights.locator: Wardle said that Meta developers made several design decisions

insights.claim: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has publicly claimed Muse is 'built from the ground up for privacy and security' and published two blog posts in two weeks defending its design, but the discovered zero-day and Wardle's assessment directly contradict this messaging.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: A gap between a Big Tech company's public security claims and an independent researcher's findings is a reputational and regulatory risk factor for Meta as it pushes deeper into agentic AI products.
insights.quote: To me, the bar is infinitely higher in terms of the security of these apps. They don't have to be perfect, but when you take a look at Muse, it's like they didn't, in my opinion, think about security, which is really worrisome... At the very least, they should be thinking about security from the very start, and they are just not.

insights.claim: Meta's defensive blog posts about Muse's security design come amid a wave of separate revelations that internal testing of AI models from Anthropic and Google resulted in security breaches of external, unintended third-party networks — actions that in traditional human hacking could result in criminal charges.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: This situates Muse's vulnerability within a broader industry pattern of frontier AI agents causing unintended real-world security incidents, a systemic risk theme across multiple major AI labs, not isolated to Meta.
insights.locator: The posts come amid revelations that internal testing of models

insights.claim: Meta representatives did not respond to emailed questions about the vulnerability, and the article concludes that, contrary to Meta's claims, Muse 'can't be trusted' and it's unclear if or when it ever can be.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: A blunt 'can't be trusted' verdict from a technical security outlet on a flagship consumer AI product is a strong negative signal for near-term enterprise/consumer trust and adoption of Muse specifically and Meta's agentic AI roadmap broadly.
insights.quote: Like most such AI agents—and contrary to Meta's claims—Muse can't be trusted. It's not clear when or if it ever can.
insights.locator: As already noted, the extraordinary access Muse requires

insights.claim: Amazon began blocking Muse from being used to shop on its site roughly 12 hours before Wardle publicly disclosed the zero-day, telling users Muse is an 'unauthorized AI agent' that violates Amazon's Conditions of Use, and stating it wants third-party purchasing agents to operate openly and respect merchants' participation decisions, comparable to how food-delivery and travel-booking apps must respect the businesses they interact with.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: A major e-commerce platform proactively blocking an AI shopping agent signals an emerging industry conflict over agentic commerce access rights, a governance issue likely to affect other AI-agent shopping products beyond Muse.
insights.quote: We think it's fairly straightforward that third-party applications that offer to make purchases on behalf of customers from other businesses should operate openly and respect service provider decisions about whether or not to participate.
insights.locator: Amazon said in an emailed statement

insights.claim: Muse can book appointments, fill out forms, handle customer service, make purchases, generate images, create documents, and connect to a user's WhatsApp, email, calendar and social media accounts, and can create new tools on the fly when a task requires one that doesn't exist, but the macOS app currently has no Windows version.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: The breadth of account and OS-level access Muse requires to function is precisely what makes its security flaws high-impact; the platform-exclusivity (macOS only) also currently limits Meta's addressable market for the product.
insights.locator: Meta introduced Muse a few weeks ago
